findings.issue: InternalFeignConfig only adds X-Internal-Token. The global CorrelationAndAuthForwardingInterceptor (libs/common-web) still runs on CartInternalFeignClient, so on the inline attempt (attemptClearCart, which runs on the checkout request thread) the user's bearer token is sent to POST /internal/carts/{userId}/consumed. The relay runs on the scheduler thread, so it sends no bearer. cart-service's /internal/** chain ignores Authorization and the target is the in-cluster service that already gets this token through CartFeignClient, so nothing is newly exposed. It still breaks the brief's rule that the internal client must not forward the user's bearer, and no test pins the rule.
findings.fix: Strip Authorization for internal-token clients: add a per-client interceptor or Capability that runs after the global one and calls template.removeHeader("Authorization"), or have the global interceptor skip templates that carry X-Internal-Token. Add a test that asserts a CartInternalFeignClient request made inside a request context carries X-Internal-Token and no Authorization.

findings.issue: removeConsumed calls lockOrCreateCart(userId), so any internal call, including a relay retry or an admin retry of a DEAD row for a user whose data was erased after the order, inserts a new cart.carts row keyed by that user_id. The endpoint can therefore recreate a record linked to an erased user, and it accepts unknown user ids (the test expects 200 for a random UUID).
findings.fix: Lock the existing cart without creating one, for example SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on cart.carts WHERE user_id = :u. When there is no cart, return removed=0 so the outbox row still goes DONE.

findings.issue: The CLEAR_CART payload holds userId, orderId and, for each line, productId, variantId, offerId, quantity and addedAt. It contains no direct PII (no name, email or address), but it is per-user behavioural data. It is kept in orders.outbox indefinitely, including DONE rows, and the privacy erasure flow does not touch orders.outbox. last_error and the relay WARN/ERROR logs carry only the kind, the aggregate id (a v3 UUID derived from the user id) and the exception text, never the payload.
findings.fix: Null or minimise the payload when a CLEAR_CART row goes DONE, or purge DONE CLEAR_CART rows after N days, and add orders.outbox payloads that reference the user to the order-service erasure step. A note in the privacy docs would cover the residual retention.

summary: No blockers or majors. The new POST /internal/carts/{userId}/consumed sits behind cart-service's HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE /internal/** chain (InternalSecurityConfig). That chain fails closed when the token is blank (expected.length > 0) and compares tokens in constant time with MessageDigest.isEqual. There are tests for 401 with no token, a wrong token and an unconfigured token. The gateway has discovery.locator.enabled=false and no Path predicate under /internal. The new GatewayEdgeIntegrationTest checks that an anonymous caller gets 401 and an authenticated caller gets 404, and that the request is not proxied. Validation meets CTO condition 3: UUID path, @Valid, lines capped at 50 with @NotNull elements, quantity from 1 to 99, @NotNull addedAt, and orderId is never used for scoping. The DELETE uses bound parameters and is scoped to the cart_id resolved from the path userId. It matches product, variant_key, offer_key, quantity and addedAt to the millisecond, and the unique key (cart_id, product_id, variant_key, offer_key) means each line removes at most one row, so at most 50 per call. A holder of the internal token is trusted by design and can only remove exact matches in the named user's cart. There is no user-facing IDOR because the path is internal-only. A replay cannot wipe a newer cart: lines added or changed later have a different addedAt or quantity, and the enqueue is idempotent per order (ON CONFLICT on idem_key). CLEAR_CART rows use a per-user aggregate, a name-based UUID that cannot collide with order ids, so a stuck clear only holds back that user's later clears, never payment or order events. For WALLET, the enqueue is inside the same transaction as markPaid and ORDER_PLACED, after the debit, and adds no new failure mode beyond the existing markPaid and publish insert. The inline attempt runs after commit and swallows errors. The relay caps CLEAR_CART at a 240 s backoff and 400 attempts, and every other kind keeps its limits. The order-side client uses InternalFeignConfig, so a blank token is sent as blank and fails closed at cart-service. There are no new secrets. The only new dependency is the test-only spring-boot webmvc-test. The three minor findings are: the user's bearer still reaches the internal endpoint on the inline attempt through the global forwarding interceptor; lockOrCreateCart can recreate a cart row for an erased or unknown user; and CLEAR_CART payloads are retained without erasure coverage.
